text_en: After Paul and Silas had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
text_cn: 保禄和息拉经过安非颇里和阿颇罗尼雅，来到得撒洛尼，在那里有犹太人的会堂。

text_en: And Paul went in, as was his custom, and on three sabbath days argued with them from the scriptures,
text_cn: 保禄照常例，到他们那里，一连三个安息日，根据圣经和他们辩论，

text_en: explaining and proving that it was necessary for the Messiah to suffer and to rise from the dead, and saying, “This is the Messiah, Jesus whom I am proclaiming to you. ”
text_cn: 阐明指出默西亚必须受难，并从死者中复活；且说：“我向你们所传报的耶稣，就是默西亚。”

text_en: Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, as did a great many of the devout Greeks and not a few of the leading women.
text_cn: 他们中有些人信服了，便与保禄和息拉联合，还有许多敬畏天主的人和希腊人，以及不少的显贵妇女。

text_en: But the Jews became jealous, and with the help of some ruffians in the marketplaces they formed a mob and set the city in an uproar. While they were searching for Paul and Silas to bring them out to the assembly, they attacked Jason’s house.
text_cn: 但是，犹太人却起了嫉妒的心，聚集了一些市井败类，结伙成群，扰乱城市；又闯进雅松家里，搜寻保禄和息拉，要拉他们到民众那里。

text_en: When they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some believers before the city authorities, shouting, “These people who have been turning the world upside down have come here also,
text_cn: 但没有搜到，就把雅松和几个弟兄，拉到本城官长前，呐喊说：“这些扰乱天下的人，也到这里来了，

text_en: and Jason has entertained them as guests. They are all acting contrary to the decrees of the emperor, saying that there is another king named Jesus. ”
text_cn: 雅松竟收留了他们；这些人都背叛凯撒谕令行事，说另有一位国王，就是耶稣。”

text_en: The people and the city officials were disturbed when they heard this,
text_cn: 他们使群众和本城官长们听了这事，都惶惶不安。

text_en: and after they had taken bail from Jason and the others, they let them go.
text_cn: 本城官长便由雅松及其余的人取了保状，便将他们释放了。

text_en: That very night the believers sent Paul and Silas off to Beroea; and when they arrived, they went to the Jewish synagogue.
text_cn: 弟兄们便立即在夜间打发保禄和息拉去贝洛雅； 他们到了那里，就进了犹太人的会堂。

text_en: These Jews were more receptive than those in Thessalonica, for they welcomed the message very eagerly and examined the scriptures every day to see whether these things were so.
text_cn: 这里的人比得撒洛尼人开明，接受这道，极其热切，天天考究圣经，看这些事是否是真的。

text_en: Many of them therefore believed, including not a few Greek women and men of high standing.
text_cn: 所以他们中有许多人信从了，还有许多希腊尊贵妇女，男子也不少。

text_en: But when the Jews of Thessalonica learned that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Beroea as well, they came there too, to stir up and incite the crowds.
text_cn: 可是，得撒洛尼的犹太人，一知道保禄在贝洛雅也传开了天主的圣道，就到那里煽动扰乱群众。

text_en: Then the believers immediately sent Paul away to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained behind.
text_cn: 弟兄们遂立即打发保禄往海边去；息拉和弟茂德仍留在贝洛雅。

text_en: Those who conducted Paul brought him as far as Athens; and after receiving instructions to have Silas and Timothy join him as soon as possible, they left him.
text_cn: 送保禄的人领他一直到了雅典；他们领了保禄的命令，叫息拉和弟茂德赶快来到他那里，以后就走了。

text_en: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply distressed to see that the city was full of idols.
text_cn: 保禄在雅典等候他们时，见城里满是偶像，心神很是悲愤。

text_en: So he argued in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and also in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
text_cn: 所以他就在会堂里，同犹太人和敬畏天主的人辩论，每天也在街市上，同所遇到的人辩论。

text_en: Also some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers debated with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say? ” Others said, “He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign divinities. ” (This was because he was telling the good news about Jesus and the resurrection. )
text_cn: 有几个伊壁鸠鲁派和斯多噶派的哲士同他争论，有的说：“这个饶舌多言的人想说什么？”有的说：“看来他是个外国鬼神的宣传者”──因为保禄宣讲耶稣及复活的福音。

text_en: So they took him and brought him to the Areopagus and asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
text_cn: 他们遂带保禄，领他到了阿勒约帕哥，说：“我们可以知道你所讲的这新道理是什么吗？

text_en: It sounds rather strange to us, so we would like to know what it means. ”
text_cn: 我们听见你说了一些新奇的事，所以我们想知道这到底有什么意思。”

text_en: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners living there would spend their time in nothing but telling or hearing something new.
text_cn: 原来所有的雅典人和侨居在那里的外国人，不管其他的事，只是论谈或探听一些新奇的事。

text_en: Then Paul stood in front of the Areopagus and said, “Athenians, I see how extremely religious you are in every way.
text_cn: 保禄遂即站在阿勒约帕哥当中说：“众位雅典人，我看你们在各方面都更敬畏神明，

text_en: For as I went through the city and looked carefully at the objects of your worship, I found among them an altar with the inscription, ‘To an unknown god. ’ What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.
text_cn: 因为我行经各处，细看你们所敬之物，也见到一座祭坛，上面写着“给未识之神。”现在，我就将你们所敬拜而不认识的这位，传告给你们。

text_en: The God who made the world and everything in it, he who is Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in shrines made by human hands,
text_cn: 创造宇宙及其中万物的天主，既是天地的主宰，就不住人手所建的殿宇，

text_en: nor is he served by human hands, as though he needed anything, since he himself gives to all mortals life and breath and all things.
text_cn: 也不受人手的侍候，好像需要什么似的，而是他将生命、呼吸和一切赏给了众人。

text_en: From one ancestor he made all nations to inhabit the whole earth, and he allotted the times of their existence and the boundaries of the places where they would live,
text_cn: 他由一个人造了全人类，使他们住在全地面上，给他们立定了年限，和他们所居处的疆界；

text_en: so that they would search for God and perhaps grope for him and find him—though indeed he is not far from each one of us.
text_cn: 如他们寻求天主，或者可以摸索而找到他；其实，他离我们每人并不远，

text_en: For ‘In him we live and move and have our being’; as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are his offspring. ’
text_cn: 因为我们生活、行动、存在，都在他内，正如你们的某些诗人说的：“原来我们也是他的子孙。”

text_en: Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the deity is like gold, or silver, or stone, an image formed by the art and imagination of mortals.
text_cn: 我们既是天主的子孙，就不该想：神就像由人的艺术及思想所制的金银石刻的东西一样。

text_en: While God has overlooked the times of human ignorance, now he commands all people everywhere to repent,
text_cn: 天主对那愚昧无知的时代，原不深究；如今却传谕各处的人都要悔改，

text_en: because he has fixed a day on which he will have the world judged in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed, and of this he has given assurance to all by raising him from the dead. ”
text_cn: 因为他已定了一个日期，要由他所立定的人，按正义审判天下，他为给众人一个可信的凭据，就叫这人从死者中复活了。”

text_en: When they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some scoffed; but others said, “We will hear you again about this. ”
text_cn: 他们一听见死人复活，有的讥笑，有的却说：“关于这事，我们后来再听你罢！”

text_en: At that point Paul left them.
text_cn: 这样，保禄便从他们当中出去了。

text_en: But some of them joined him and became believers, including Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
text_cn: 可是，也有几个人依附保禄而信从了，其中有阿勒约帕哥的官员狄约尼削，和一个名叫达玛黎的妇人；同他们一起信从的，还有其他一些人。
